Note API Reference¶

Back to PlussQit API Reference

This is the per-method reference for pluss::Note — one page per method, in the same handwritten, compiled-and-verified style as the rest of the PlussQit object references. For building a Note, see the separate Note Factory API Reference; everything on this page assumes a Note already exists.

What Note Is¶

Note is PlussQit’s low-level, homogeneously typed value family for text work. A defined Note has one dtype — Text, Bytes, Bool, Int64, or Float64 — and a shape of rank zero through three. Text methods consume text or byte cells; predicates, measurements, comparisons, and scores remain Notes by changing the result dtype instead of abandoning shape and ownership for a host container.

Reach for Note when the data are strings, tokens, lines, snippets, prompts, document fragments, or LaTeX, and the work is cleanup, matching, rewriting, splitting, tokenization, regex extraction, or text-oriented natural-language preprocessing.

How The Methods Are Shaped¶

Most Note methods preserve shape and act cell by cell: a rank-1 Note of three cells maps to a rank-1 Note of three cells. A few families break that mould:

  • Predicates — contains, starts_with, ends_with, the is_* character-property checks (is_alpha, is_digit, is_blank, and the regex() accessor match/search predicates return a shape-preserving Bool Note. Compose masks with &, |, ^, and ~; cross the host boundary explicitly with bools() only when native contiguous lanes are required.

  • Measurements — lengths_bytes, lengths_chars, lengths_graphemes, and count_substring return a shape-preserving Int64 Note. integers() exposes its contiguous lanes without copying.

  • Variable-length structural results — split, split_lines, split_whitespace, the regex accessor’s findall, and the line/character difference methods return a TokenBatch: one flat Text/Bytes Note (batch.tokens()) plus an Int64 Note (batch.offsets(), shape [numel + 1]) that marks where each input cell’s run of tokens begins and ends in the flat stream. Row r’s tokens are tokens.at(k) for k in [offsets[r], offsets[r + 1]). These are methods of the result object, not root Note methods; the complete result contract lives in the TokenBatch API Reference.

  • Linguistic operations — nlp() opens the dedicated Note NLP Accessor API Reference for tokenization, cleanup, extraction, scoring, phonetics, alignment, and language-oriented set comparison.

  • Regular expressions — regex() opens the dedicated Note Regex Accessor API Reference for whole-cell matching, substring search, counting, extraction, rewriting, and splitting.

  • TeX/LaTeX source — tex() opens the dedicated Note TeX Accessor API Reference for TeX-aware cleanup, math-delimiter handling, construct removal, environment extraction, macro expansion, math simplification and standardization, format conversion, and structural/semantic extraction.

  • Shape & layout — reshape, flatten, squeeze, unsqueeze, transpose, permute, and contiguous change rank or axis order without touching cell content; repeat copies complete patterns across dimensions, while repeat_interleave makes adjacent copies along one selected axis.

  • Cell access & ownership — at and at_indices borrow one cell as a std::string_view; cell, cell_at, and owned return a TextRef that keeps the packed arena alive; host materializes rank-aware owning standard-library strings.

  • Structural projections — scalar and vector are explicit borrowed text boundaries; matrix and slabs return storage-sharing row or slab Notes and therefore preserve dtype and ownership; sizes_view borrows extents without allocating.

Running The Examples¶

Every example is a runnable fragment (assume #include <pluss/pluss.h> and #include <iostream>), and every ### Output block is copied verbatim from a permanent compiled reference executable. Those verifiers cover cell access, structural projections, collection ordering, operators, Boolean reductions, structural repetition, and targeted masking; their saved transcripts are compared byte for byte with fresh executable output during documentation work.

To print a Note, any of these render byte-identical text, and the pages rotate through them:

std::cout << pluss::note::print(n) << "\n";  // print(n) -> std::string
std::cout << n << "\n";                       // operator<< (default options)
pluss::note::print(std::cout, n) << "\n";     // print(os, n) -> the stream

Typed Note results can be printed without first extracting host storage:

// Bool and Int64 results preserve n's shape.
const auto mask = n.contains("x");
const auto lengths = n.lengths_bytes();
std::cout << mask << '\n' << lengths << '\n';

// A TokenBatch contains two Notes.
const auto batch = n.split(",");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.offsets()) << "\n";

Examples that show a rejection call the method inside a try block and print the first line of pluss::Error::what() (the message); what() also appends a Triggered at: location line, which the output blocks omit.

Coverage¶

This reference documents the methods users reach for first:

  • Metadata and rank — defined, dim, size, sizes, numel, empty, is_scalar, is_vector, is_matrix, and is_rank3.

  • Case — lower, upper, casefold, title, capitalize, swapcase.

  • Boundary trimming — strip, lstrip, rstrip.

  • Whitespace & layout — collapse_whitespace, collapse_spaces, collapse_newlines, collapse_repeats, collapse_punct, dedent, indent, remove_control_chars, to_ascii.

  • Unicode normalization — to_nfc, to_nfd, to_nfkc, to_nfkd, strip_accents, strip_bom, strip_zero_width, normalize_quotes, normalize_dashes, normalize_ellipsis.

  • Character-class filters — remove_punctuation, remove_symbols, remove_digits, remove_letters, remove_emojis, keep_alnum, keep_alpha, keep_digits, keep_ascii, keep_printable.

  • Rewriting — replace, replace_first, replace_last, replace_n, remove, remove_all, remove_prefix, remove_suffix, ensure_prefix, ensure_suffix, surround, quote, unquote.

  • Inspection — contains, contains_any_alpha, contains_any_digit, starts_with, ends_with, count_substring, is_alpha, is_alnum, is_digit, is_lower, is_upper, is_title, is_whitespace, is_blank, is_ascii, is_utf8_valid, is_bytes, lengths_bytes, lengths_chars, lengths_graphemes.

  • Value algebra — + concatenates Text or Bytes cells, * repeats cell contents, comparisons return Bool Notes for every dtype, and &, |, ^, and ~ compose Bool Notes. any and all reduce a complete Bool Note to a rank-zero Bool Note.

  • Structural tokenization — split, split_lines, and split_whitespace. Pattern extraction lives on the regex() accessor, while linguistic tokenization and sentence analysis live on the nlp() accessor.

  • TeX/LaTeX source — cleanup, extraction, conversion, and rendering live on the tex() accessor.

  • Transport encodings — base64_encode/base64_decode, hex_encode/hex_decode, url_encode/url_decode.

  • Escaping — html_escape/html_unescape, json_escape; TeX escaping lives on the tex() accessor (tex().escape()/tex().unescape()).

  • Encoding & transcoding — to_utf8_strict, to_utf8_lossy, from_latin1/to_latin1_lossy, from_windows1252/to_windows1252_lossy — convert between a bytes-mode payload and UTF-8 text.

  • Linguistic analysis — cleanup, masking, extraction, transliteration, phonetics, scoring, and token comparison live on the nlp() accessor.

  • Shape & layout — reshape, flatten, squeeze, unsqueeze, transpose, permute, contiguous. These are metadata-only: the cell strings are untouched, only the rank and axis order change.

  • Selection & slicing — select (one slab along an axis, that axis dropped), narrow (a contiguous range along an axis, rank kept), take (gather cells by an index list, rank-1 result).

  • Collection reduction & ordering — join reduces all text cells to a scalar Note, join_flat extracts one owning standard string, sort orders lanes, argsort returns the Int64 positions of that order, unique returns sorted distinct values or slices, and deduplicate keeps their first-seen order.

The root remains focused on storage, shape, and general text mechanics. The NLP accessor has its own A-Z method reference and navigation chain.
